title: Is this chip block ready to manufacture?
prompt:
Create a large 16:9 landscape infographic for a general professional audience (managers, engineers new to the topic, students), light near-white background, warm and clear like a well-designed museum explainer or a quality newspaper graphic. Plain everyday language is the main text; technical names appear only as small grey secondary labels.

TITLE (large): "Is this chip block ready to manufacture?"
SUBTITLE: "How TOKN checked six chip building blocks against the four tests that must pass before a design is sent to the factory."

BAND 1 — heading "Why this matters": one wide card with a simple flat illustration of a silicon chip die with a grid of circuit blocks, and this text: "Sending a chip design to the factory ('tapeout') costs millions and takes months. A block that fails timing or wiring checks after tapeout means starting again."

BAND 2 — heading "Who did the work": a left-to-right flow of eight round role badges joined by arrows. Each badge shows a line icon, the bold role name, the short description in quotes, and the model name tiny and grey below:
1 Scout — "lists the tools available" (claude-haiku-5.5) [icon: binoculars]
2 Planner — "writes what 'done' looks like" (claude-opus-5.5) [icon: document]
3 Analyst — "runs the official checks" (Kimi-K3.1-Pro) [icon: bar chart]
4 Skeptic — "re-checks and finds 14 weak spots" (FW-GLM-5.3) [icon: shield]
5 Judge — "decides: revise or ship?" (Microsoft-Decision-1) [icon: balance scale]
6 Editor — "fixes every weak spot" (gpt-6.1-sol) [icon: pencil]
7 Coach — "writes a lesson for next time" (claude-opus-5.5) [icon: lightbulb]
8 Examiner — "scores it with plain code, no AI" (verify.py) [icon: checklist]
Caption under the flow: "Like a newsroom: a writer, a fact-checker, an editor — and an exam nobody can sweet-talk."

BAND 3 — heading "Four tests every block must pass": four cards in a row, each with an icon, the question in large plain words, and a tiny grey tool label:
(floor-plan grid icon) "Is the block packed too tightly to wire up?" — tiny grey label: floorplan
(stopwatch icon) "Do signals arrive in time?" — tiny grey label: static_timing
(ruler and set square icon) "Does the layout follow the factory's drawing rules?" — tiny grey label: drc_check
(two matching circuit diagrams icon) "Does the layout match the circuit diagram?" — tiny grey label: lvs_check

BAND 4 — heading "What it found": 6 result cards in a row. Each shows the small ID at top, a large verdict word in its color with a matching status icon, and one plain sentence:
BLK-CPU — green (#16A34A) verdict "Ready" — "All four tests pass."
BLK-DSP — green (#16A34A) verdict "Ready, just" — "Exactly on the packing target, and timing closes at exactly zero."
BLK-USB — red (#DC2626) verdict "Fails" — "Layout and circuit diagram differ in 2 places."
BLK-SRAMCTL — blue (#2563EB) verdict "Ready, with a caveat" — "Packed at 82% against an 80% target: wiring may be crowded."
BLK-DMA — red (#DC2626) verdict "Fails" — "Signals arrive 0.003 ns late."
BLK-PCIE — amber (#D97706) verdict "Can't judge" — "No timing constraints were supplied, so timing can't be checked."
Small note at the right of the heading: "One failed test is enough to stop a block."

BOTTOM BAND — three short panels:
"Trust, but verify" — "An independent checker re-ran the checks and plain code graded the result: 6 of 6 correct."
"Honest wording" — "Its confidence covers applying the rules to these records, not working silicon."
"Getting better each run" — "The lesson saved for next time: Copy each tool result exactly; a negative timing margin is a failure even without an error."

FOOTER (small, centered): "The takeaway: 0.003 ns late is still late. The factory doesn't round down."

TEXT DISCIPLINE: use ONLY the words given above in quotes plus the headings. Do NOT add any slogans, taglines, mottos, handwritten notes, brand lines, decorative words, extra footers or invented statistics. Every word spelled exactly as given and legible at 4K.

Visual rules: generous whitespace, strong hierarchy (title > band headings > plain sentences > tiny grey technical labels), verdict colors only on the result cards, soft blue/teal section tints, flat friendly line icons. No people, no faces, no photos.
